I can’t change your email account’s system settings from here, but I can make everything you send (or draft) in German and help you set up templates, replies, and a message to IT requesting a permanent preference change. Here are practical options — tell me which you want me to do and any preferences (formal vs. informal tone, use “Sie” or “du”, include signature details, etc.):

Options I can do for you now
1) Translate and save the appointment-request draft into German (I already saved a draft earlier). I can update that draft so it’s ready to send in German.
2) Create a set of German templates / canned responses (formal business templates: meeting request, follow-up, thank-you, contact update, out-of-office).
3) Offer to translate any outgoing email into German before sending (I’ll draft/send the German version).
4) Draft an email to your IT/helpdesk asking them to change your mailbox/clients default language to German (I can save it as a draft or send it).
5) Create a German out-of-office autoreply message (if you want the text to use in your email client).
6) Convert your email signature into German and save it as a template for you to paste into settings.

Quick examples (formal, using “Sie”):
- Formal greeting: "Sehr geehrte/r Frau/Herr [Nachname],"
- Opening sentence: "Ich hoffe, es geht Ihnen gut. Ich möchte gern einen Termin vereinbaren..."
- Closing/sign-off: "Mit freundlichen Grüßen," or "Freundliche Grüße,"
- Signature template:  
  [Ihr Vorname Nachname]  
  [Position]  
  [Firma]  
  Tel.: [Telefonnummer]  
  E-Mail: [E-Mail-Adresse]

What I need from you
- Do you want formal (“Sie”) or informal (“du”)?  
- Any specific signature details to include?  
- Should I update the existing appointment draft to German now?

Tell me which action(s) to take and your tone/signature preference — I’ll proceed.
